# `⌾` — Under

When `g` only selects or rearranges, `f⌾g Y` puts the result of `f(g Y)` back where `g` took it from. The rest of `Y` is unchanged. `g` qualifies when [selective assignment](assign.qmd) accepts it as a target: Take, Drop, Replicate, Reverse, Transpose, Ravel, Enlist, Pick and `⌷`, with Each, Rank, Axis or an atop of them.

```bpl
-⌾(1 0 1#)1 2 3         ⍝ ¯1 2 ¯3
+\⌾∊ [3 1 0] [2 5]      ⍝ [[3 4 4] [6 11]]
9⌾(0⌷) 1 2 3            ⍝ 9 2 3
```

For any other `g`, `f⌾g Y` is `g⁻¹(f(g Y))`. `X f⌾g Y` is `g⁻¹((g X)f(g Y))`.

```bpl
3+⌾ 2× 4           ⍝ 7
⌽⌾ 1+ 1 2 3        ⍝ 3 2 1
⌊⌾ 10× 1.25        ⍝ 1.2
```

Call order: `g Y`, `g X`, `f`, then `g` on the positions of `Y`, or `g`'s inverse.

See [Inverse pair](inverse-pair.qmd).

## Errors

- `DOMAIN`: `g` neither selects nor has a known inverse
- `LENGTH`: the result of `f` doesn't fit the selection
